Writ Appeal is filed under  Clause 15 of the Letters Patent against the order passed by this Co  W.P(MD)No.6818 of 2021 dated 10.11.2023.
 For Petitioner : Mr.B.Elankumaran  For R  1 : Mr.S.Karthik  For RR 2 & 3 : Mr.M.Sarangan  Additional Government Ple  ORDER (Order of the Court was made by J. NISHA BANU, J.) C.M.P(MD)No.17548 of 2023 has been filed to grant leave to the petitioner to file the Writ Appeal against the order passed by the learned Single Judge in W.P(MD)No.6818 of 2021 dated 10.11.2023.
2.Heard the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner, the learned counsel appearing for the first respondent and the learned Additional Government Pleader appearing for the respondents 2 and 3 and perused the materials placed before this Court.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

( Uploaded on: 20/03/2025 11:33:39 am )
3.The petitioner, who is a third party in the Writ Petition, has filed the petition to grant leave to him to file the Writ Appeal, wherein the first respondent herein has filed the Writ Petition directing the respondents to release the full compensation amount to him for the property comprised in S.F.No.574/1A, Kodalvavee Village, Dindigul West Taluk, Dindigul, whereby and whereunder, the writ Court passed the following order:
3.When the matter is taken up for hearing today, the learned Special Government Pleader appearing on behalf of the respondents submitted that the compensation has already been ascertained and it is broadly calculated under three heads.
The first head is land, the second head is building and the third head is the expenses that will be incurred for relocation of the machineries.
The learned Special Government Pleader submitted that there was some dispute between the petitioner and the above said T.Sivakumar.
Due to this inter se dispute, the second respondent was not able to pay the compensation amount.
4.The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that he does not have any objection in paying compensation to the tenant under the head of relocating the machineries.
He further submitted that the tenant had left huge arrears payable towards electricity consumption and also rent.
Therefore, it was contended that this amount must also be deducted from the compensation payable to the tenant and the balance can be given to the tenant.

T.Sivakumar vs R.Palanichamy on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131996387/
2 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 20/03/2025 11:33:39 am )
5.In the considered view of this Court, the inter se dispute between the petitioner and his tenant cannot be handled by the respondents.

sentences.text: The arrears that is claimed by the petitioner towards consumption of electricity and rental arrears should be independently recovered by the petitioner from the tenant and that cannot be a subject matter while paying the compensation.
In view of the same, the compensation with regard to the land and building can be paid to the petitioner and the compensation for relocation of the machineries can be paid to the tenant.
Insofar as recovery of the electricity dues and rental arrears, the petitioner has to independently proceed against the tenant.

6.In the result, this writ petition is disposed of with a direction to the respondents to pay the compensation for the land and building to the petitioner and for the relocation of the machineries to the tenant.
This process shall be completed within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
The petitioner shall place his title documents before the first respondent to clarify that he is entitled to receive the entire compensation towards the land and building.
Copy of the award passed shall also be furnished to the petitioner by the second respondent.
No costs.
Aggrieved over the same, the petitioner has filed the Writ Appeal.

4.It is an admitted fact that the petitioner herein is a tenant and on perusal of the materials available on record, it is seen that there is a dispute between the petitioner herein and the first respondent/landlord https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 20/03/2025 11:33:39 am )
regarding payment of the compensation amount, wherein acquisition proceedings were initiated under the National Highways Act.
Since there is a civil dispute between the parties, the petitioner has to approach the competent civil forum and therefore, we are not inclined to entertain the grant leave petition.
Accordingly, this petition is dismissed.
No costs.
Consequently, connected W.A(MD)SR.No.94551 of 2023 is rejected, at the S.R stage itself.
